purpose: Diagnose, without promotion or parameter selection, whether any preregistered linear mixture between the P0685 local generator and P0690 fully routed source produces viable raw RX J2129 image topology.

equation.boundary: fixed-RAR point-mass boundary shared by both endpoints

registered_marker.meaning: P0691 baryonic quadrupole value; included as a labeled marker, not selected from this atlas

nuisance_fit.source_positions: two coordinates profiled independently for seven spectroscopic families on training images
nuisance_fit.continuum_seed_rule: use the identical P0691 optimizer starts for every fraction so basin changes are not confused with source-mixture changes
nuisance_fit.map_interpolation: bicubic; no ellipticity, rotation, radial amplitude, mass sheet, gravity amplitude, photon amplitude, or slip is fitted

global_topology.critical_curve_present: at least one horizontal or vertical sign-changing determinant cell
global_topology.parity_diverse: at least one positive and one negative determinant root

decision_rule.promotion: No row may advance, be selected, or be described as validation evidence.
decision_rule.retire_sampled_linear_family: yes if zero preregistered rows pass every diagnostic viability gate
decision_rule.if_any_row_is_viable: report the interval only as a behavior that a future baryon-derived local geometric law must predict; freeze that new law before any new score
decision_rule.if_no_row_is_viable: retire linear mixtures of these two endpoint sources and move to a spatially varying or non-linear source operator
decision_rule.sealed_targets: P0633 and P0640 remain sealed regardless of atlas outcome

claim_boundary: Every target outcome in this atlas is spent RX J2129 development evidence.
A passing row would be post-hoc diagnostic evidence and cannot become a selected universal parameter.
Finite sampling cannot mathematically exclude an arbitrarily narrow interval between rows.
The zero-slip photon closure remains diagnostic rather than a relativistic metric theory.
